 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Marshall-Edgeworth price index equals** 155.92.
 
• The Marshall-Edgeworth index is a price index used to measure changes in the price level between two periods.
 
 
• It is based on the Laspeyres price index formula and is used to adjust for changes in both the quantity and quality of goods over time.
 
 
 
• The formula for the Marshall-Edgeworth index is:

 ME = ((∑p1q0) +(∑p1q1))/((∑p0q0) +(∑p0q0))times 100= (395 +422)/(260+264) times 100= 155.92
